slot.brief: A block on a smooth incline inside a lift accelerating upward with known a; resolve forces along/perpendicular to incline and find acceleration relative to incline.

stem: A smooth incline at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal is fixed inside a lift accelerating upward at $2$ m s$^{-2}$. A block is released on the incline. Taking $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, what is its acceleration relative to the incline?

verdicts.working: In the lift frame, effective gravity is 12 m s^-2 downward. The component down the smooth incline is 12 sin 30° = 6 m s^-2.

working:
$g_{\text{eff}}=g+a_{\text{lift}}=12$ m s$^{-2}$
$a_{\parallel}=g_{\text{eff}}\sin30^\circ=12\times\dfrac12=6$ m s$^{-2}$

Independent check: In the lift frame, effective gravity is 12 m s^-2 downward. The component down the smooth incline is 12 sin 30° = 6 m s^-2.
solution:
In the lift frame, the effective gravitational acceleration is $g_{\text{eff}}=g+a_{\text{lift}}=10+2=12\,\text{m s}^{-2}$ downward.
$$a_{\text{relative}}=g_{\text{eff}}\sin30^\circ=12\times\frac12=6\,\text{m s}^{-2}$$
Thus, the block accelerates down the incline at $6\,\text{m s}^{-2}$.
